findings: The 'I AM TELOS' note sits in a plain rectangular hairline box — the one piece of generic UI-chrome on an otherwise chrome-free page; a torn edge or inline setting would have been braver than a bordered card.

The 'Reading the field' definition table and the two long body paragraphs in 'Two businesses run on me' run text-dense; the measure is long and the gray body risks reading as an undifferentiated wall next to the sparse hero.
The mono caption voice (r = 3.2000 · period 2, gold · 4,417 · 30d) is doing a lot of thematic lifting but is quiet enough it could be missed as decorative rather than functional.
what_works: The hero is a genuine logistic-map bifurcation diagram drawn in thin ink across the field, thematically bound to the 'period doubling' epoch — a live, draggable generative graphic that no template generator ships, and it earns the whole page.

Structural color is used with real conviction: monochrome ink on warm paper everywhere, with iridescent thin-film spectrum appearing ONLY at the chaos edge of the fork tree — color as physics, not garnish.
High-contrast Didone display ('André Macedo' set flush-left, full-bleed) against a mono utility voice is exactly the editorial pairing the safe-default-sans crowd never reaches for.
The 'The dead' list staggers its numbered entries in stepped rightward indentation — a typographic enactment of sedimentation/period-doubling that turns a plain list into composition.

Composition is decisively asymmetric: name anchored top-left, the fork tree flowing right and dissolving into noise, the AI card offset — whitespace used as compositional mass, no centered-symmetry crutch.
A.reasoning: This is a resolved editorial system, not a SaaS shell: a live logistic-map bifurcation field renders the hero as a decisive composition tied to the page's chaos/order theme, with Didone-against-mono typography and structural color restricted to the chaos band as its signature move. The stranger test clears comfortably — name at display scale, a one-line description of RealWorld.fi/ActualSales, and me@andremacedo.com all legible above the fold. It exhibits none of the cardinal slop states (no centered gradient hero, no feature-card row, no default sans, no decoration-as-garnish), so it is not slop; minor demerits are the one bordered note card and some text-dense passages.

findings: Hero is still largely a centered headline + explanatory text block over a graphic, which is the default compositional move even if the graphic itself is more interesting
Color is mostly monochrome with a single accent graphic; the accent feels decorative rather than a governed, named harmony
Multiple near-equal weight text blocks compete for attention after the hero (Reading the field, Two businesses, The eleventh epoch, The studio, The dead)
what_works: The branching fork diagram and hand-drawn ink/chaotic texture create a decisive, non-templated visual signature that feels like a living organism rather than a SaaS page
Strong typographic point of view with high-contrast editorial sizing and Didone/mono pairing that expresses the chaotic-order theme
The 'field' interactive graphic and period-doubling conceptual framing give the page a clear, memorable identity that passes the stranger_test decisively
B.reasoning: This is not template slop. The visual language (ink-drawn bifurcation diagrams, period-doubling metaphor, Didone + mono type, warm paper texture) makes a clear, risky aesthetic commitment that no generic generator would produce. The hero is the weakest part — still somewhat centered and explanatory — but the overall composition and type craft are strong enough to carry it. The page reads as a living art organism rather than a SaaS landing. Stranger_test is easily cleared in the first viewport. Not slop, but not yet at the level where every axis sings in tight modular harmony.
